children: Bank of England policymaker Megan Greene said the risks of a pickup in broader inflation as a result of the energy price shock from the Iran war were greater than the BoE expected and she reiterated her view that interest rates should go up.

Greene – part of a minority on the BoE's Monetary Policy Committee that has voted for higher rates – said it was better to act as if the so-called second-round effects from the energy shock were stronger and then adjust policy later if needed.

"I therefore continue to believe we should proactively lean against the risk of second-round effects," she said in the text of a speech she was due to give at the London School of Economics on Tuesday.
